src.label: USDA APHIS — pet travel from the United States to Korea (relaying Korean quarantine rules)

head: Korea expects a microchip, a current rabies vaccine and a rabies antibody test of 0.5 IU/ml or more.
lines: The US agriculture department page on Korean entry rules says a dog or cat needs a current rabies vaccine given before arrival, a rabies neutralising antibody test of 0.5 IU/ml or higher, and an ISO-compliant microchip. Pets under 90 days old need neither the vaccine nor the test.

From the US the health certificate must be issued by an accredited vet and endorsed within 30 days of export. If the chip or the antibody test could not be done before shipping, they can be done after arrival in Korea, but the animal will likely be held in quarantine at the owner's expense until they are finished.
This is a US-side relay, not the Korean quarantine agency page, so check the Korean agency before travel.
